g.title: dependencies
g.text: 31 results and 2 remarks; arrows point from prerequisites to consequences

a.xlink:title: Reuse the proof of Corollary 3.3, replacing its numerical input by Proposition 3.4.
For real $N,X\ge1$, the height average of the second moment over $N\le\lvert n\rvert<2N$ is $\ll_\varepsilon (NX)^\varepsilon NX^2$. Both frequency signs are included.
For $N,X\ge1$ and $0<\delta\le1$, restricting the moduli to $(Y,(1+\delta)Y]$ gives the height-mean bound $\ll_\varepsilon (NX)^\varepsilon X^2\{N\delta+\min(1,N\delta^2X)\}$.

For $a,\kappa,\eta>0$ and $X\ge2$, outside a set of Lebesgue measure $O_{a,\kappa,\eta}(X^{1-\kappa+\eta})$, the bound $\mathcal K_2(N;Y)\le3NX^{2+\kappa}$ holds simultaneously for every real $1\le N\le X^a$.

For $X\ge2$, the height average of $\mathcal D_Y+\mathcal D_Y^*$ is $\ll_\varepsilon X^{-2+\varepsilon}$. Each discrepancy is at least $\lfloor Y\rfloor^{-2}$ for every $Y\ge2$. The supremum over rectangles is inside the average.
For $\kappa,\eta>0$ and $X\ge2$, both discrepancies are at most $X^{-2+\kappa}$ outside a set of Lebesgue measure $O_{\kappa,\eta}(X^{1-\kappa+\eta})$.

For $X\ge2$, the positive distance moments have orders $X^{-s}$ for $0<s<2$, $X^{-2}(\log X)^2$ for $s=2$, and $X^{-1-s/2}$ for $s>2$. The covering radius lies between $\tfrac12X^{-1/2}$ and $4X^{-1/2}$.

For integer $Q\ge2$, $1/2\le\tau<1$ and $L=\tau Q^2$, an exact sinc-squared weighted second moment isolates determinant-one Farey pairs. Its asymptotic is $LN_Q+(12\tau/\pi^2)I(\tau)Q^4+O(Q^3\log(2Q))$, uniformly in $\tau$, with $I(\tau)>0$.

For every sufficiently large integer $Q$, some symmetric interval with radius $T\asymp Q^2$ has a second-moment remainder whose absolute value is $\gg Q^4$. The constants are absolute; this is an existence statement for the interval.

Records the inverse Kuznetsov formula for both signs and the local spectral large sieve on a window of width $G$, for $N,T\ge1$ and $1\le G\le T$. The formula uses the signed measure $dm=\chi\,dm_0$; the large sieve uses positive $dm_0$.
Deduces a dual second-moment estimate $\ll_\eta F^2TG(TG+N)^{1+\eta}$ for a spectral-window integral with a multiplier bounded by $F$, for either sign.
Records the uniform-in-$r$ twisted Bessel estimates in the imaginary range $\lvert t\rvert\ge1$ and the holomorphic range $k\ge1$. The low imaginary spectrum is treated separately in Lemma 2.4.
For $\lvert t\rvert\le1$ and $Z>0$, both twisted transforms are $\ll_V1+\log^+(1/Z)$, uniformly in the real twist $r$.
For all integer $m,n$ and $c\ge1$, $\lvert S(m,n;c)\rvert\le(m,n,c)^{1/2}c^{1/2}\tau(c)$.
Expresses $S(m,n;c)$, for integer arguments, as a divisor sum of Kloosterman sums with one argument equal to one. The cumulative form is equation (2.6).
Consecutive fractions of Farey order $Q\ge1$ have determinant one and denominators whose sum exceeds $Q$.
For frequencies separated by $\lambda$ modulo one and any integer interval of length $H\ge1$, the absolute error from $H\sum_j\lvert y_j\rvert^2$ is at most $\lambda^{-1}\sum_j\lvert y_j\rvert^2$.

Bounds rectangular discrepancy of a nonempty finite sequence in $\mathbb T^2$ by a Fourier sum and a truncation term, allowing repeated points and closed or half-open arcs, including empty and full arcs.

For a fixed smooth compactly supported $W$, $C,N\ge1$ and real $r$, the second moment of the twisted smooth sums $B_\sigma(n,r)$ is $\ll_{\varepsilon,W}(NC(1+\lvert r\rvert))^\varepsilon(N+1+\lvert r\rvert)$.
Proves the moving-interval height mean at a base height $C\ge1$, with the factor $N\delta+\min(1,N\delta^2C)$. Theorem 1.2 is the corresponding formulation with signed frequencies.
For $N,X\ge1$, inserting the weight $1/c$ in the cumulative sums gives height-averaged second moment $\ll_\varepsilon(NX)^\varepsilon N$.

For $M,N,X\ge1$, the height-averaged second moment over $\lvert m\rvert\le M$, $\lvert n\rvert\le N$, excluding $(0,0)$, is $\ll_\varepsilon(MNX)^\varepsilon MNX^2$. Both coordinate axes are included.

With the weight $1/c$, the same frequency rectangle has height-averaged second moment $\ll_\varepsilon(MNX)^\varepsilon MN$. The proof of Corollary 3.3 is reused with Proposition 3.4 as the input estimate.
For $Y\ge2$ and integer $K\ge1$, controls $\mathcal D_Y$ by weighted squared Fourier coefficients and $1/K$, and proves $\mathcal D_Y^*\le\mathcal D_Y+1/N_Y$.
If integers $Q,R\ge1$ satisfy $2QR\le X$, every product of open consecutive Farey gaps of orders $Q$ and $R$ contains a lift of a point of $\mathcal P_X$.

For $0<\rho\le1$ and irrational $x$, controls the least Farey order $R_\rho(x)$ giving a gap of length at most $\rho$. It proves the range $\rho^{-1/2}\le R_\rho(x)\le2/\rho$ and a quadratic tail estimate.

Bounds the tail of $\rho R_\rho(x)R_\rho(y)$ by a quadratic decay times the smaller of two logarithmic factors, for $1\le z\le4/\rho$; above this range the tail is empty on irrational-coordinate pairs.
For $X\ge2$ and $t>0$, the measure of $\{d_X>t\}$ is $\ll [1+\min\{\log(2+Xt),\log(2+1/(Xt^2))\}]/(X^2t^2)$.
Gives an explicit arithmetic inequality in the denominators of the rational corner and the side lengths that makes two oppositely oriented open rectangles empty of lifts of $\mathcal P_X$.

For $X\ge2$ and $-2<s<0$, the distance moment has order $X^{-s}$. For $s\le-2$ it diverges. The three assertions use disc counting, the positive first-moment upper bound, and a local singularity, respectively.
For integer $Q\ge2$, $M\in\mathbb Z$ and integer $H\ge1$, the second moment over $M<n\le M+H$ differs from $HN_Q$ by at most $Q(Q-1)N_Q$.
For real $L\ge2$, the absolutely convergent Fourier series of $w(n/L)$ equals the triangular kernel $L(1-L\lVert\theta\rVert)_+$ for every real $\theta$.

For integer $Q\ge2$ and real $L\ge Q^2/2$, evaluates the weighted second moment as the diagonal term $LN_Q$ plus the contribution of determinant-one Farey pairs. The correction vanishes for $L\ge Q(Q-1)$.
For $1/2\le\tau<1$, reduces $I(\tau)$ to a one-dimensional integral and proves it is positive. On $[1/2,5/8]$ it gives the explicit lower bound $1/9000$.
